rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at moderate temperature to elute all 8 compounds and map the overall elution window without risking truncation. This should reveal whether peaks are compressed early or late and guide narrowing the phi window and adjusting slope in the next injections.

The only failure is a very close pair around 7.37–7.39 min, so first test whether that pair is slope-sensitive by making the gradient much shallower while keeping the same phi window and temperature. If resolution improves substantially, we can then shorten from there; if it barely changes, we will know to shift temperature or the phi window instead.

The close pair is strongly slope-sensitive: at 20 min it coelutes, while at 40 min all pairs are resolved but too slow. Interpolate to a shorter gradient near the expected resolution threshold to keep all pairs above 1.5 while bringing the last peak back toward 10 min.

The critical pair remains unresolved at 24 min but is fully resolved at 40 min, so bracket the threshold with 32 min at the same window and temperature. This should show whether full resolution can be achieved with a smaller time penalty than 40 min.

Since slope changes trade one critical pair against another, the next lever is temperature to alter selectivity rather than gradient steepness. Dropping to 25 C should increase retention modestly and may separate the close pair(s) while likely keeping the last peak near or below 10 min.

At 25 C the method is nearly optimal, with only one pair slightly below 1.5 and just a small time penalty. A modest increase in gradient time should lift that pair over the threshold while keeping t_last close to 10 min, likely improving CRF further.

Twenty minutes at 25 C is almost ideal but just misses full resolution, so test a small temperature increase to fine-tune selectivity without the larger time penalty of a longer gradient. This may move the critical pair above 1.5 while keeping the last peak close to or under 10 min.

Temperature clearly changes selectivity, and 30 C created a new early critical pair while 40 C shifted the problem later; 35 C will map the crossover between these regimes. This helps locate whether a narrow temperature window can give all pairs acceptable resolution at about the same fast run time.

Since 20 min at 25 C is the current best and already close to the optimum balance, the next step is to see whether a slightly steeper gradient can keep the same near-complete resolution while pulling the last peak closer to 10 min. This directly tests whether the best point lies just shorter than 20 min rather than longer.

The peaks elute within a fairly narrow effective phi range, so trimming the high end of the gradient should slightly shallow the slope where the compounds elute and may improve the critical mid-run pair without much time cost. Using phi1 0.90 is a conservative first window-narrowing step that should still keep all compounds inside the gradient.

Raise phi0 one step while keeping the successful 20 min, 25 C conditions to trim unused weak solvent and slightly shorten the run. If selectivity is preserved, this could reduce t_last toward 10 min and improve on the current best CRF.

Injection 11 is essentially optimal, with only one pair just under 1.5 and almost no time penalty. A 2 min longer gradient at the same phi window and temperature should push that pair over 1.5; if t_last stays close enough to 10 min, this is the best chance to reach CRF 1.000.

Injection 11 shows the sweet spot is very near full resolution at 10 min, so the next refinement is to narrow the gradient window slightly at the high end while keeping the same tG and T. This should shallow the effective slope enough to lift the 3/4 pair over 1.5, while the higher phi0 may keep t_last at or very near 10 min.

Injection 11 is just shy of perfect mainly because t_last is barely above 10 min and one pair is marginal, so raise phi0 one more step to shorten retention while preserving the successful broad upper window. This tests whether a slightly stronger start can keep all pairs at or near full credit and bring the last peak to 10 min or below.

At phi0 0.15 the run is fast enough, so now trim phi1 one step to shallow the gradient and target the marginal 3/4 pair without reintroducing a time penalty. This combination has the best chance to keep t_last under 10 min while nudging the last unresolved pair above 1.5.

Now that all pairs are fully resolved with t_last under 10 min, the only possible improvement is to confirm whether the method can be shortened further before a pair drops below 1.5. Reducing tG to 18 min is the most direct test of the time-resolution edge from the current optimum.

The 20 min, 25 C method is already optimal by CRF, so use remaining budget to map robustness around the optimum. Raising temperature one step at the same phi window will show whether full resolution survives a modest T change or whether the critical pair is highly temperature-sensitive near the chosen method.

The optimum at 0.15/0.90/20/25 has margin in the last peak time, so a slightly narrower gradient window may still keep all compounds within the gradient while potentially improving selectivity around the critical pair. This tests whether the perfect method can be made more efficient in solvent window without sacrificing CRF.

The perfect method likely sits near the current phi window, so test a stronger starting composition with the same slope class to see whether retention can be reduced further while preserving full resolution. This probes whether the optimum has a broader plateau or whether the critical pair quickly degrades when phi0 is increased beyond 0.15.

Use a longer gradient to see whether the temperature-induced early coelution at 30 C can be recovered by shallower slope at the otherwise optimal phi window. This characterizes robustness and confirms that selectivity, not just gradient steepness, is what makes 25 C uniquely optimal.

The optimum is already found, so use the remaining budget to test the opposite temperature direction around that method. Lowering temperature one step while slightly lengthening the gradient will show whether there is a broader fully resolved region below 25 C or whether 25 C is truly the selectivity maximum near this phi window.

A slightly narrower window at 20 min gave full resolution with only a tiny time penalty, so now test whether shortening that shallower window restores t_last below 10 min while keeping all pairs resolved. This is the most plausible nearby alternative to the current perfect method.

Since 0.15/0.85/18/25 also reaches CRF 1.000 with only modest resolution margin on the critical pair, test one more step narrower at the high end to identify the edge of the fully resolved plateau. This will show whether the method can be made still more focused without losing the perfect score.

The 0.15/0.80/18/25 method gives perfect score with good resolution margin, so raise phi0 one step while keeping the narrowed window and short gradient to probe the fastest nearby fully resolved region. This tests whether the same 1.000 CRF plateau extends to a stronger starting composition.

The 0.15/0.80/18/25 method still has full resolution with the last peak just under 10 min, so one final step narrower at the high end cleanly tests the boundary of the 1.000-CRF plateau. If it holds, this defines an even tighter fully resolved window; if not, 0.80 is confirmed as the edge.
